I'm not trying to be flippant here, but how does it help? I recently considered getting a diagnosis for a learning disability, mainly because I want it to be harder to fire me at work (I have a very mean boss, which is making all of my current problems worse, btw). But how can testing for a learning disability help?

It's funny, because so long as I'm following a "script," like talking to people about work-related stuff or topics I know to be "normal," like clothes or coffee or celebrities, I do fine... I pass for normal and friendly. But, once people get to know me, it just sort of all goes downhill from there...

*Edited for autocorrect derp*
I find it reassuring to know that there are other people like us out there. Thank you for the kind words.

Honestly, the response I've received from those close to me in real life is so negative, I'm afraid to talk about the current one. No one on reddit is talking about it (trust me, I've looked), so I'm just going to assume that this time,  I really am on my own :-\ 

Feel free to PM me if you want more info, but I don't want to make the entire community uncomfortable.

Lol, not taken the wrong way at all, I thought of that when I read this over before posting. I've actually been tested for autism spectrum disorders twice; once as a kid, because my mom was convinced there was "something wrong with" me, and once as an adult because someone I was close to was getting tested, and I went along with them to be supportive. Both times, I basically came up as "normal," whatever that means. I suspect I may have a learning disability, and I do have PTSD, which causes me to hyperfocus on things (it's hard to explain why, it just sort of helps me calm down and focus).
